text:
alex: quick sync — we need a lightweight playbook for onboarding new catalog models that balances customer-driven pins vs catalog stability. thinking: 3 acceptance gates (perf, regressions, infra) + an opt-in migration path for customers who want early access. suggestions?
maria: +1. customers keep asking for faster upgrades but fear regressions. they want a 2 week opt-in window before auto-swap. can we commit to that? :thinking_face:
ken: can we be explicit about metrics? propose: latency p95 change <= +20ms, generation quality regressions < 2% on our primary eval set, and token-cost delta < 10%. if any fail -> hold.
sarah: + metrics look reasonable. add a safety gate: reversible pin for 7 days post-swap with automated rollback if error rate spikes. define error as user-visible failure rate or SLO breach.
josh: ops question — how do we run canaries? recommend: 1) internal canary (10% internal traffic) 2) early customer opt-ins (20% of opted customers) 3) gradual ramp to 100% over 72h. also, need a quick checklist for infra: quantized variant availability, KV cache compatibility.
priya: for benchmarks we should separate microbench (latency/cost) vs semantic-eval (QA/LLM eval). microbench runs on standard sequences (64, 256, 1024). semantic-eval uses the pinned prompt-suite + customer holdout prompts. include minimum sample sizes.
alex: ok — draft playbook idea:
```
- Stage 0: model ingest + basic compatibility tests (tokenizer, weights ok)
- Stage 1: infra microbench (p95, throughput, memory) -> must pass thresholds
- Stage 2: semantic eval vs baseline (regression suite + customer holdouts)
- Stage 3: internal canary + triage window (48h)
- Stage 4: opt-in customer migration (2 weeks opt-in) + monitor
- Stage 5: gradual default swap (72h ramp) + 7-day reversible pin
```
maria: love it. what about customer communication? need templated emails + Console flag for "early access". also billing note: mention cost delta when they opt-in.
ken: we need automated signals + thresholds wired into console dashboards: quality-regressions, user-satisfaction proxies (CTR, re-rank feedback), latency/cost deltas. alert if any exceed thresholds.
sarah: edgecases — model variants. if quantized variant causes >3% quality drop we should auto-fallback to FP16 variant until fix. add compatibility layer in routing.
josh: ops: add a final pre-swap check command we can run: `./canary-check --model new --baseline old --suite canonical` that returns pass/fail + diagnostics. link it to deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: canary-check started for model `catalog/model-eta-v3` against `model-eta-v2` (suite: canonical). ETA: 15m.
priya: timeline request — can we aim to have this playbook and the first run for eta-v3 by EOW? customers are lining up. if not EOW then next Tue.
alex: let's aim EOW. action items: ken -> define numeric thresholds and dashboard panels (due 48h). priya -> prepare eval suites & run baseline (due 48h). josh -> add canary-check command + ops runbook (due 72h). maria -> draft customer comms and Console flag copy (due 72h). sarah -> rollback policy doc + routing rules (due 72h). i'll own final playbook and publish.
maria: noted. ping me on PR. :thumbsup:
ken: starting thresholds doc now.
priya: kicking off eval runs, will paste results into this thread.
deploy-bot: canary-check finished: pass=partial, failures=2 tests (semantic suite). see logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/2141590000
alex: thanks bot — priya/ken can you triage failures? if semantic fails we hold the opt-in.
priya: looking. initial quick look: both failures are hallucination cases on long-context prompts; sending examples.
ken: if it's long-context failure we should add a targeted regression test and block until fixed. propose a focused canary with longer context lengths only.
sarah: agree, block default swap until long-context patch. keep opt-in open for willing customers but flag the risk in comms.
josh: ops — will mark model `eta-v3` as "opt-in allowed" and disable default routing. also set monitoring high-sensitivity for hallucination signals.
alex: good. we'll reconvene after triage. thanks all.
